program.name: Backend mentoring, cohort 4
program.description: A six-month structured mentoring programme pairing early-career backend engineers with senior engineers across Africa and the UK. Pairs meet twice a month and work towards one substantial project.
program.timeCommitment: About two hours a month for six months.
program.eligibility: Open to women and non-binary engineers with less than three years of professional experience. Mentors need at least five years.

sections.title: About you
sections.description: The basics. Nothing here is scored.

fields.label: What should we call you?
fields.help: The name your mentor will see.

fields.label: Where are you based?
fields.help: City and country is enough. We use it to find an overlapping working day.

fields.label: When would you like to start?
How many years have you been writing code?
fields.help: Count anything, including learning on your own.

fields.label: What has been hardest to work out on your own?
fields.help: Two or three sentences. There is no right answer and this is not a test.

fields.label: What would you like to work on?
What would make this six months worth it?
fields.help: Say it in your own words. Plain is better than polished.

fields.label: How confident do you feel about your next career step?
How often would you like to meet?
Attach a CV, if you have one
fields.help: PDF or Word, up to 5 MB. Not having one will not count against you.

00000008-0000-4000-8000-000000000001.body: Hello Amara, thank you for taking me on. I have been building a small expense tracker in Flask.
Good to meet you Blessing. Send me the repository when you get a chance and I will read through it before we talk.
Shared it now. The part I am least sure about is how I structured the database layer.
I read it. The structure is reasonable. What I would change first is moving the queries out of the route handlers, so the routes only handle the request and response.
That made a real difference. Routes are about ten lines each now.
Good. Next thing worth learning is writing a test for one of those functions. Pick the one you were most nervous about changing.
Wrote three tests. One of them caught a bug where I was not handling an empty result.
Also wanted to ask about how you decided to move into payments work.

00000008-0000-4000-8000-000000000002.body: Hello Fatima. Before we meet, tell me what you are working on and what you would like to be doing in a year.
I am learning Python on my own. In a year I want to be working as a backend engineer.
That is a clear goal. Let us pick one project and take it further than feels comfortable, rather than starting several.
Agreed. I will finish the library API I started.
Send it over when the first endpoint works end to end.

00000008-0000-4000-8000-000000000003.body: Hello Tobi, looking forward to working together. What would be most useful to start with?
Thank you. I will come back with something specific this week.

00000008-0000-4000-8000-000000000004.body: Hello Grace. You said Java and system design. Which of the two is closer to what you need this month?
System design. I can write Java but I freeze when someone asks me how I would build something.
Then we will draw. Every session, one system on paper before any code.
Drew the ticketing one on my own this week and it held together.
That is the cohort finished. You came in unable to start a diagram and you are now finishing them unprompted. Keep drawing.

milestones.title: First conversation
milestones.description: Both sides have met once and agreed how often they will talk.
milestones.strandPrompt: Have you two managed a first conversation yet? Agreeing how often you will meet is most of the work.

milestones.title: Goals agreed
milestones.description: The mentee has named what they want out of the six months.
milestones.strandPrompt: What does the mentee want to be able to do by the end? Write it down here, even roughly.

milestones.title: Halfway review
milestones.description: A check that the pairing is working, while there is time to fix it.
milestones.strandPrompt: You are halfway. What has been useful, and what would you change for the second half?

templates.subject: You are in, {participant.firstName}
templates.body:
Hello {participant.firstName},

You are on the roster for {programme.name} at {organisation.name}. Matching runs on {programme.matchingDate}, and you will hear from us either way that day.

There is nothing you need to do until then. If your profile is not finished, finishing it is the one thing that improves your match.

templates.subject: You have been matched with {partner.firstName}
templates.body:
Hello {participant.firstName},

You have been matched with {partner.firstName} for {programme.name}.

The first conversation is the hardest one to arrange and the one that decides whether the rest happen. Open your strand and send them a message today if you can.

templates.subject: It has been quiet in your strand
templates.body:
Hello {participant.firstName},

You and {partner.firstName} have not spoken in a couple of weeks. That is normal and it is not a failure.

If the timing has stopped working, say so — rearranging is easier than starting again.

templates.subject: Halfway through {programme.name}
templates.body:
Hello {participant.firstName},

You are halfway through {programme.name}. We ask everyone the same two questions at this point: what has been useful, and what would you change.

It takes two minutes and it is what tells us whether to change anything for the second half.

templates.subject: {programme.name} has finished
templates.body:
Hello {participant.firstName},

{programme.name} has come to an end. Thank you for the time you gave it.

Your strand stays open to read back over. If you and {partner.firstName} want to keep talking, nothing here stops you.

mergeCodes.description: The other side of their strand

broadcasts.subject: Matching runs on 14 September
broadcasts.body:
Hello {participant.firstName},

Matching for {programme.name} runs on 14 September. If your profile is not finished, this week is the week.

broadcasts.subject: Ten minutes on your profile
broadcasts.body:
Hello {participant.firstName},

Your profile is not finished, and matching works on what you tell us. Ten minutes now is the difference between a good match and a guess.
